reviewers.summary: The new test exercises sign-out and sign-in, but it does not verify preservation of an active in-scope case across a session change. The prior test-coverage finding remains unresolved.

findingList.message: The session-change test does not cover retaining an in-scope active case. Sign-out clears that selection, and the next session puts cp-case-b first, so the test passes when selection always falls back to the first scope.

evidence.codePathTraced: Clicking Sign out calls handleSessionChange(null), which clears selectedCaseId. The subsequent sign-in therefore has no active case to retain and falls back to the first case scope.
evidence.failureScenario: If session-change handling always selects the first scope, this test still passes: the new session lists cp-case-b first, so the assertion sees Case cp-case-b even though the user’s prior selection was cleared at sign-out.

reviewers.summary: The added test still cannot detect the previously reported regression in production session-change handling. Its sign-out/sign-in sequence clears the selected case before the new session is applied.

findingList.message: The session-change test does not prove retaining the active in-scope case: it signs out, clearing the selection, then signs in to a session whose first scope is already cp-case-b. Exercise a non-null session change while cp-case-b is selected, with another scope first, and assert cp-case-b remains selected.

evidence.codePathTraced: The test selects cp-case-b, then signs out, which calls handleSessionChange(null) and clears the selection. On sign-in, cp-case-b is the first scope in nextSession, so the test does not verify retaining a selected case across a non-null session change.
evidence.failureScenario: If session changes always selected the first scope, this test would still pass: sign-out clears cp-case-b, and the next session selects its first scope, cp-case-b. A regression that loses an in-scope selected case during a session change therefore remains undetected.

reviewers.summary: The round-3 test exercises the session-change flow, but its case ordering lets the reported regression pass undetected. I found no security vulnerability in the changed lines.

findingList.message: The prior test finding remains: the session-change test does not detect a regression to always choosing the first case scope. Put cp-case-a before cp-case-b in nextSession.caseScopes while cp-case-b is selected, then assert cp-case-b remains active.

evidence.codePathTraced: The integration test signs in with cp-case-b selected, then changes sessions. Its next session lists cp-case-b first, so a handler that always selects the first scope still produces the asserted result.
evidence.failureScenario: If the production session-change handler regresses to always selecting the first scope, this test still passes because cp-case-b is first in nextSession.caseScopes. The test therefore does not catch the prior finding’s regression scenario, where cp-case-b remains in scope but cp-case-a is first.
